meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Canadian federal constitutional framework; Quebec civil law for private law and corporations incorporated under the Quebec Business Corporations Act; common law applies federally and in other Canadian provinces
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), including investment protections subject to its terms
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement between Canada and the European Union (CETA), provisionally applied and subject to its investment-protection framework
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-European Free Trade Association Free Trade Agreement
Canada-United Kingdom Income and Capital Taxes Convention
The applicable treaty depends on the investor's residence, ownership chain, income type, and treaty-in-force status. Quebec is not a separate treaty party.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal corporations: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 2.1 and 21.1-21.303, including the register of individuals with significant control. Quebec corporations: Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, and Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, including ultimate-beneficiary disclosure requirements administered by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. AML/CFT: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2017, c. 21; and applicable Canadian sanctions regulations. The app operator is not automatically a FINTRAC reporting entity merely because it provides software or social communications; payment, remittance, virtual-currency, foreign-exchange, or other regulated activities may independently trigger registration and AML obligations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access for federal CBCA ISC records; mixed and partially public for Quebec entities because prescribed ultimate-beneficiary information is filed with and generally searchable through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, subject to statutory exclusions, masking, and restricted personal information. Nominee arrangements do not eliminate disclosure obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or certificate of existence for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the country or province of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing jurisdiction is a Convention party; otherwise consular legalization through the destination-country diplomatic mission. Canada has implemented the Apostille Convention for Canadian public documents through competent authorities designated by province and Global Affairs Canada.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or authorized corporate records custodian in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, followed by certified translation into French where required for filing or use before Quebec authorities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, notary, company secretary, or other legally authorized issuer in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; private certificates may require notarization before authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Shareholder register, ownership chart, and ultimate-beneficiary declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder, authorized officer, regulated professional, or competent registry, depending on origin-country law

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or government identity document for each director, officer, authorized signatory, and identified ultimate beneficiary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport or national identity authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry in the country or province of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation, registry filing, or banking
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal or corporate authorized signatory before a notary or lawyer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Usually official issuance without apostille for Canadian use; foreign certificates may require Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, banking, payment onboarding, and material ownership changes, screen all direct and indirect owners, ultimate beneficiaries, directors, officers, authorized signatories, agents, major counterparties, and payment intermediaries against Canadian sanctions lists administered by Global Affairs Canada, United Nations sanctions implemented in Canada, OFAC sanctions where a United States nexus exists, and relevant domestic PEP, foreign PEP, head-of-international-organization, family-member, and close-associate databases. Apply risk-based enhanced due diligence to PEPs, opaque ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, nominee structures, adverse media, unexplained wealth, virtual-asset exposure, and cross-border payment activity. Preserve screening evidence, false-positive resolutions, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth records, and escalation decisions. Canadian sanctions and criminal prohibitions apply independently of whether a person appears on an OFAC list.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services portal for Quebec corporations: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; Corporations Canada online filing centre for federal corporations: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Quebec corporation must have a French name or an English or other-language name accompanied by an acceptable French version where required by the Charter of the French language, CQLR c. C-11, and its regulations. The name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to an existing registered name, not misleading as to legal form, purpose, affiliation, or status, and must comply with Quebec language and public-order requirements. A federal corporation may use an English, French, or bilingual corporate name, but its name must satisfy the Canada Business Corporations Act and Corporations Canada approval requirements. Transliteration does not cure lack of distinctiveness or language-law non-compliance. Trade names, app names, domain names, trademarks, and corporate names require separate searches.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Royal, Crown, King, Queen, Prince, Princess, Government, Canada, Quebec, Québec, municipal names, and terms implying governmental, Crown, diplomatic, university, banking, insurance, securities, charitable, or professional status without required consent or authorization

Bank, trust, credit union, insurance, securities dealer, investment fund, stock exchange, university, college, hospital, cooperative, charity, foundation, and similar regulated or protected expressions where sectoral approval is required
Words suggesting a connection with a public authority, Indigenous government, international organization, police, military, or another existing legal entity
Obscene, discriminatory, violent, defamatory, misleading, or otherwise contrary-to-public-policy expressions
A name confusingly similar to an existing corporate name, registered business name, trademark, domain, or reserved name
French-language forms that violate the Charter of the French language, including insufficiently French corporate presentation or non-compliant public-facing commercial usage
Use of Inc., Corp., Ltée, Limitée, or equivalent legal-form designations inconsistent with the selected statute or corporate form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain a written rejection reason and preserve the search report, proposed name, translations, consent letters, and supporting evidence. For a Quebec filing, correct the name, provide required consents or French-language justification, and resubmit through the Registraire des entreprises portal. If the decision is maintained, request administrative review or reconsideration from the Registraire and pursue the applicable review or appeal route under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the Administrative Justice Act, CQLR c. J-3, within the prescribed period stated in the decision. For a federal filing, submit revised name options or supporting evidence through Corporations Canada and use the statutory review or court remedy available under the Canada Business Corporations Act if an adverse decision is legally challengeable. A name reservation is not trademark clearance; conduct Canadian trademark, corporate-name, domain, app-store, and Quebec French-language searches before commitment.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A corporation must maintain a registered office in the applicable jurisdiction and keep statutory records at the legally required location. A commercial virtual office may be acceptable for registry correspondence if it is a genuine service address, receives official documents, and satisfies the applicable statute and filing requirements. It is not sufficient where the business requires operational premises, privacy-compliant data governance, employees, customer support, records access, payment-service controls, or regulated activities. For a real-time video-matching and social-telephony application, maintain documented Canadian or Quebec management, contractual, tax, privacy, cybersecurity, incident-response, and customer-support substance proportionate to the business model. The registered office must not be represented as a physical operating facility if no such facility exists.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-zero for a software-only business with no regulated payment activity; an indicative risk estimate is approximately 5%-15% annually for an unannounced registry, tax, licensing, or compliance-related physical verification, not a statutory probability. The risk increases materially if the entity uses a virtual office, has inconsistent address information, receives regulatory complaints, claims Quebec substance without local activity, handles payments or personal information at scale, has high-risk foreign ownership, or presents AML, sanctions, tax, or consumer-protection indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 17-49 (incorporation and organizational meetings), s. 115 (registered office), ss. 126-152 (officers and directors); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) / Constitution en personne morale
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital under the Quebec Business Corporations Act; articles may prescribe authorized share capital without a minimum paid-up contribution. No escrow account is required for a general business corporation; escrow arrangements are not triggered absent special security or professional trust account requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation accept the subscription for 1,000 common shares by the incorporator at par value, and that such shares be issued to the named subscriber upon payment. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be established at [address], Province of Quebec, and that the nominated director be authorized to effect all filings. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President/Chief Executive Officer, [Name] be appointed Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Treasurer, each to serve until successors are elected. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises (Quebec Business Registry) - online name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Nuans-style registry and trademark search to confirm that the proposed corporate name is distinctive, lawful, and not confusing with existing names. File a name reservation application through the online OneBiz portal, selecting up to three alternative names in order of preference. Pay the reservation fee and obtain a reservation certificate valid for 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a new reservation with different distinctive elements, or request an administrative review of the refusal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises (OneBiz online filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory Articles of Incorporation in French, specifying authorized share capital, registered office, director names, and any restrictions. Submit the articles electronically to the Registraire via OneBiz, pay the incorporation fee, and receive the Certificat de constitution and the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). Ensure all signatures match notarized consents if physical filing is used.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any deficiency notice from the Registraire within the stated period, correct the articles, and resubmit; request post-filing correction if the certificate contains errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organizational Meeting and Registered Office Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal) with notification to Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Call the organizational meeting and adopt the first board resolution approving share subscription, establishing the registered office at the designated address in Quebec, and appointing the president, secretary, and treasurer. Record the minutes in the corporate records book and notify the Registraire of the registered office address and first directors within the statutory notification period.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (lease or authorization letter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire queries the notice, file an amending declaration with corrected officer or address information; late filings may be cured by an application for rectification with explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Issuance and Officer Appointment Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and Board of Directors / corporate records book
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue the subscribed shares to the incorporators upon receipt of the agreed subscription price; endorse share certificates; update the share ledger and capital contribution records. Formalize officer appointments and maintain written consents in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Register of shareholders or share ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any securities record defects by a directors' resolution and reissue certificates; administrative penalties for omitted registry declarations may be rectified through a corrected return.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and General Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (Ville de Montréal or applicable Quebec municipality business permit office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence or certificate of commercial activity for the registered office and actual place of business. Provide the certificate of incorporation, NEQ, and a declaration that operations consist solely of data-processing and video-matching application services without physical manufacturing. Satisfy zoning, occupancy, and building accessibility requirements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal a municipal refusal through the municipal administrative tribunal; if only a technical omission, resubmit with the required zoning letter or drawings and pay any applicable late fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business registration online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with Revenu Québec for QST, payroll source deductions, and CNESST employer account; register with the CRA for GST/HST and corporate income tax account. Use the NEQ and federal program accounts to activate filings. If employees will be hired, complete the CNESST occupational health and safety registration and workplace injury prevention plan.
required_dossiers: Bank account details for tax refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is incomplete, file a request for amendment through Revenu Québec's online service or the CRA Business Window; reactivation of dormant accounts requires a written reconsideration request and supporting identity documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) – Quebec Economic Innovation and Energy Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence and Quebec Enterprise Registration (no sector-specific operating permit for digital data and video-matching services)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category III non-industrial information technology service; no mandatory EIA under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c E-1.1, for purely digital office-based operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial discharges; any sanitary or office wastewater must comply with municipal sewer by-laws under the Environment Quality Act; VOC and GHG emissions are limited to heating and office equipment and remain below reporting thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certificate from the local fire service; compliance with the Quebec Building Code (CQLR c B-1.1) for structural load, occupancy limits, and accessibility; CNESST workplace health and safety clearance and workers' compensation registration required before hiring employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for GST/HST and federal corporate income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec provincial corporate income tax and QST; Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) for enterprise registration and issuance of the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). Primary portals: CRA My Business Account (canada.ca) and Revenu Québec TransID (revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first register as an extra-provincial company with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain a NEQ, or use a federal incorporation with provincial registration. Subsequently, apply online or via Form RC1 to CRA for a federal Business Number (BN). Upon the BN being issued, the entity must open the applicable CRA program accounts, including the GST/HST account (RM prefix) and corporate income tax account (RC prefix). For Quebec sales tax, the registrant must use Revenu Québec's online registration service to obtain a QST account number (LM prefix). Non-resident corporations without Canadian incorporation must file Form RC4696 (Non-Resident Registration) and may need to request a lease-based Quebec establishment determination.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available under Canadian or Quebec domestic law. A Canadian business corporation is always taxed at the entity level and may not be treated as a pass-through. Relevant elections include: (1) joint election under subsection 156(1) ETA for closely related corporations to treat inter-corporate supplies as made for nil consideration; (2) the section 158.1 ETA election for exempt supplies between closely related corporations; (3) corresponding QST elections under the Quebec Tax Administration Act and the Excise Tax Act (Québec) rules; (4) for hybrid mismatch planning, the entity's classification under foreign law (e.g., IRC 7701) may be examined, but this does not create a Canadian domestic pass-through status; (5) an election may be made to apportion federal and Quebec income under provincial allocation rules where a permanent establishment exists in Quebec.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) at 5% federal and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) at 9.5% provincial, applied separately as a value-added sales tax; Quebec does not use the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies (for GST) over the current calendar quarter and the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; QST follows the same threshold for supplies made in Quebec. Cross-border digital services suppliers may be required to register under the simplified non-resident registration without threshold in certain circumstances.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not mandate real-time government-side clearance or digital stamping of standard B2B invoices. Registrants must retain and issue invoices containing prescribed data under the Excise Tax Act (CTA) and Quebec's Tax Administration Act, including supplier's registration number, amount of consideration, and tax amount, unless the supply is zero-rated or exempt. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically through CRA's GST/HST NETFILE or the Related Affairs (DSAB) system; QST returns are filed through Revenu Québec TransID. For non-resident suppliers of digital services, CRA and Revenu Québec provide a simplified non-resident registration and filing gateway; there is no API-based invoice clearance approval mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada are zero-rated under Part III of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, provided the exporter keeps satisfactory evidence of physical export from Canada and the supply is made to a non-resident recipient for removal. Services (including digital streaming or video-matching services) supplied to non-residents are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI, where the service is not performed in Canada or is performed in Canada but delivered to a non-resident who is not in Canada, and the supply is not a supply of real estate, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or certain specified services (e.g., services relating to Canadian real property or personal property). For a video-chat social app, zero-rating applies if the place of supply is outside Canada and the non-resident recipient receives the service or in respect of a business that is carried on exclusively outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CED) filed through the Canada Border Services Agency's Canadian Export Information System (CAED) / CARM portal, including the export permit number and harmonized system code
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing the physical departure and destination of goods
Inward remittance certificate or bank settlement/payment evidence demonstrating the receipt of foreign consideration for the exported goods or services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rated treatment if the registered exporter or service supplier fails to produce sufficient proof of export within the reassessment period, which is four years after a reporting period unless misrepresentation or fraud extends it to 10 years. Penalties under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec's Tax Administration Act include false statement penalties of up to 25% of the tax sought to be avoided, interest on unpaid tax, and administrative monetary penalties for failure to retain records. Wilful evasion carries criminal liability, fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded, and imprisonment. Clawbacks are retroactive, and the taxpayer must pay both the tax and penalties, with no statutory grace period for late-filed export documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada; foreign-exchange control powers are statutorily allocated to the Department of Finance Canada under the Currency Act, with OSFI (prudential supervision of banks) and FINTRAC (reporting supervision under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act) completing the regulatory perimeter.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The CAD is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts and Canada adheres to IMF Article VIII. No exchange-control authorization is required for profit remittance, intercompany loans, or user-payout settlement. Controlling acquisitions by non-Canadian investors are screened under the Investment Canada Act. Outbound dividends are exposed to Part XIII federal withholding tax (25% statutory; treaty-reduced to 5% for a qualified 10% shareholder under the Canada-United States Convention) plus Quebec's complementary levy on dividends paid to non-residents by a corporation domiciled in Quebec.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not operate an export-proceeds surrender regime. No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to foreign-currency receipts generated by software, telephony, or data-processing services. Repository banks must file FINTRAC Cross-Border Wire Transfer Reports (CBR) for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, but the treasury retains full discretion over currency denomination, reinvestment, and conversion timing.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD and USD multi-currency treasury concentration)
Operational Account (primary Quebec corporate treasury; CAD/USD multi-currency)
Operational Account (US-dollar payout rail and app-store settlement ledger)
Operational Account (USD concentration and cross-border cash management)
Capital Escrow Account (contractually ring-fenced user-refund reserve established by merchant-acquiring agreement)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as the primary treasury anchor; permissible only as a payout-aggregation overlay. An offshore digital EMI (e.g., a UK or EU-authorised electronic-money institution) must be registered with FINTRAC as a foreign money services business before dealing in Canada and, after September 8, 2025, must hold a Bank of Canada payment-service-provider registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act if it executes payment functions in Canada. The EMI is not an OSFI-regulated deposit-taker and balances are not CDIC-insured. Consequently, the Schedule I bank account remains the depository and tax-basis ledger, while the EMI can reconcile App Store net settlements and fractional payout wire legs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A hybrid mandate applies. At least one signing officer must attend an in-person interview at a Quebec branch of the tier-1 bank unless the entire executive team and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) base is Canadian-resident, in which case full video-KYC is available. Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced rating, the bank will require notarized corporate resolutions, a current Registraire des entreprises du Québec extract, a complete UBO register, and a Quebec legal counsel or notary coordinates dossier. Onboarding lead time is 15 to 30 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Combined non-resident UBO concentration exceeding 10% of issued shares with no prior Canadian banking footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Quebec ultimate-beneficiary register; notarized shareholders' register; certified articles of incorporation and bylaws; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for each UBO; board resolutions appointing the signatories; FATCA/CRS self-certification forms; and business-name search results from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Paymentwall and Apple IAP as the sole monetization rails, obscuring underlying consumer-facing counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant-of-record agreements; Paymentwall's current AML/ATF compliance attestation; Apple Developer Program agreement demonstrating Apple as merchant-of-record; transaction-flow diagram; projected settlement volumes; chargeback-control policy; and daily reconciliation dashboards for app-store payouts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk video-app typologies: video-chat monetization, geo-location matching, and virtual gifting, which may trigger adverse-media and sanction-list screening failures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Terms of service and community standards; platform-level geo-blocking and OFAC-sanction-list screening policy; age-gating compliance records; anti-fraud algorithm white paper; privacy policy harmonized with Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector; customer due diligence procedures for merchants and content creators; and an independent security or vulnerability audit report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound cross-border capital in USD from a related foreign entity without a clear corporate treasury purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share-subscription agreement or intercompany loan agreement; transfer pricing documentation (contemporaneous records of cost allocation or contribution); financing board minutes; an arm's length interest schedule documenting compliance with section 247 of the Income Tax Act (Canada); and a loan-repayment schedule to substantiate the debt-equity classification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execute SWIFT MT103 from the offshore funder bank with Field 70 containing 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION / CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN - ADVANCE' plus the corporate treasury reference. The beneficiary account is held at the tier-1 clearing bank (National Bank of Canada or Royal Bank of Canada), which settles CAD through Lynx and USD through its US correspondent (Fedwire/CHIPS). FINTRAC Cross-Border Wire Transfer Reporting is triggered automatically at the CAD 10,000 threshold. No capital-import license is required, but source-of-wealth letters, funding board minutes, and loan agreements must be retained for at least four years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier, infrastructure, and content-creator payouts use SWIFT MT103 standard cover payments with ISO 20022 structured remittance information. High-value licensing or infrastructure contracts may be supported by an irrevocable commercial letter of credit under UCP600, sight or 90-day usance, as contra-security. Domestic CAD vendor payments clear through ACSS; USD payments roll through the bank's US ACH/Fedwire clearing hub. Paymentwall payout waterfalls must preserve the remittance narrative and be accompanied by a works-order of evidence to substantiate the underlying trade in goods or services.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter CAD/USD deliverable FX forwards (tenor 1 to 24 months) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex
CAD/USD vanilla FX options (single-journey premium) to cap adverse conversion on seasonal app-store and advertising settlement flows
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) matched to the tenor of the intercompany loan used for the capital injection

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to illiquid or restricted payout currencies (e.g., CNY, TRY, RUB) facing the social-telephony user payout portfolio, executed only through a licensed bank authorized counterparty
Foreign-currency spot and standing-instruction swaps for daily cash concentration between the CAD and USD operating ledgers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec Enterprise Registration Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Quebec Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days after the anniversary date of the corporation's registration with REQ
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to a monetary penalty and interest; if a declaration remains unfiled after the statutory window, REQ may issue a 60-day notice of intention to strike off. Continued default beyond that notice results in cancellation of the enterprise registration and administrative dissolution of the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) — category of corporation status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the corporation's CBCA date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive fiscal years can lead the Director to issue a notice of intended dissolution; dissolution is completed if the arrearage remains for the statutory notice period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal Corporate Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — including Quebec schedule alignment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers penalties under Income Tax Act s. 162: 5% of the outstanding tax balance plus 1% per full month of delay (capped at 12%); interest at prescribed rates; habitual failure can result in collection enforcement and winding-up proceedings initiated by CRA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (CO-17) and Annual Registration Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the CO-17 provincial corporation income tax return, due within 6 months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial late filers are assessed a penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month, capped at 12 months, plus interest; persistent non-filing may lead to suspension of Quebec business licences and prescribed collection measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Quebec Business Corporations Act and CBCA require a licensed auditor except where all shareholders consent in writing to dispense with the audit for a given fiscal year. Public or distributing corporations cannot waive the audit. There is no general revenue/asset numeric threshold for private corporations in Quebec, but regulated industries may have mandatory engagement requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; private business corporations in Quebec may use Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: In Quebec the annual declaration is the vehicle to confirm the corporation's registered office, director composition, and enterprise identification data. Share transfers are recorded in the share register within 15 days and need no separate REQ filing unless the information on directors, head office, or legal representatives changes. For CBCA corporations, the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) must be examined each year and updated within 15 days of any change, with a confirmation of 'no significant individual' when applicable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Securities Register and Beneficial Ownership Record (including Individuals with Significant Control where CBCA applies)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120–300 per year for provincial registered agent and registered office services in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000–5,000 per fiscal year for a small non-public business corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Quebec general corporate rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); Canadian-controlled private corporations on active business income may benefit from a reduced combined rate of 12.2% through the Small Business Deduction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2% on active business income up to CAD 500,000); Scientific Research and Experimental Development Investment Tax Credit; Quebec R&D tax credits and media development incentives; no broad sectoral tax holiday for ISIC 6311.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return – filed electronically through Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) e-services (GIFI included).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; federal tax instalments are quarterly where federal tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within 180 days after the fiscal year-end; instalments due on or before each quarter's prescribed monthly dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue (GIFI code 9951), cost of sales, operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canada-source gross revenue; non-resident-owned corporations must isolate income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before taxes, capital cost allowance (CCA), taxable dividends received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim eligible CCA classes and non-capital loss carry-forwards; be mindful of limitations on loss continuity upon foreign control acquisition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax payable after small business deduction and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled corporations are ineligible for the Small Business Deduction; Part I and Part XIV rates apply based on permanent establishment status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-capital and capital loss carry-forward/back calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-capital losses carry forward 20 years and back 3 years; capital losses only offset capital gains and carry forward indefinitely.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of non-arm's length transactions with non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory where aggregate cross-border reportable transactions exceed CAD 1 million; attach contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under s. 162(1) ITA: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12%; 50% gross negligence penalty for false statements or omissions; prescribed daily interest on unpaid amounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return – filed electronically via Revenu Québec eServices.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; Quebec instalments required where tax payable exceeds CAD 2,500.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal return due within six months after the taxation year-end; instalment dates follow Quebec's schedule, generally monthly for larger corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed under federal and Quebec harmonized rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income attributed to a Quebec permanent establishment; foreign tax credit on Form CO-17-V.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec tax credits, including Small Business Deduction and R&D credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quebec SBD generally unavailable to non-resident-owned corporations; claim treaty-based reductions on Form CR-1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec tax and contribution sur l'assiette générale (DGE); dividends paid to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident payees must supply a valid certificate of residency; payer files DGE schedule to reduce Quebec withholding under the applicable tax treaty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12%; 20% repeated omission penalty; monthly prescribed interest; director liability for unremitted amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Federal Part XIII statutory rate 25%; Quebec additional statutory withholding on dividends paid to non-residents 12%; combined statutory 37%. Tax treaties may reduce the combined rate (e.g., Canada–US: 15% general, 5% for a 10% corporate shareholder).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must submit a valid Certificate of Residency (TRC) issued by the home tax authority, complete CRA Form NR301 when claiming treaty exemption, and execute Form R621 (payer-side) for reduced withholding. For Quebec, use Revenu Québec Schedule DGE and Form AR-DGE; the payer must maintain sufficient ownership and substance to satisfy limitation-on-benefits clauses.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Federal Part XIII: 25% on interest (arm's length interest generally exempt) and 25% on royalties; Quebec adds 12% withholding on royalties paid by Quebec-resident corporations; Canada–US treaty generally reduces interest to 0% (arm's length) and royalties to 10% (or 0% for certain copyright royalties), with Quebec relief dependent on the same DTA and administrative forms.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 and contemporaneous Local File documentation are mandatory where aggregate non-arm's length cross-border transactions exceed CAD 1 million; a Master File is required for MNE groups with consolidated global revenue of CAD 760 million or more (Country-by-Country Reporting threshold).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations in Canada/Quebec; however, CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245 ITA), business purpose test, and beneficial ownership analysis; a Quebec video-matching corporation must maintain real office premises, local board decisions, and operational substance to avoid treaty shopping denial or sham recharacterisation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful evading of corporate tax, suppressing video-platform subscription revenue, creating fictitious expenses, or misreporting cross-border service payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 239 ITA criminal sanctions: fine up to 200% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years; gross negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax under s. 163(2); Quebec criminal and civil penalties under Taxation Act ss. 1020–1029.1.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted as parties to the offence, subject to personal fines, restitution orders, and imprisonment; CRA may issue third-party demand and enforce director liability under s. 227.1 for unremitted source deductions, plus travel bans pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file T106, absence of contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, or artificial pricing of subscription, licensing, or digital-ad services to a foreign related hub.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 247(3) ITA penalty: 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment (minimum CAD 5,000); CRA may reassess outside the normal reassessment window; outstanding tax and interest remain collectable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are generally not liable for the TP penalty unless they cause or participate in a false entry; however, they may be pursued for unpaid corporate tax under CRA civil collection if the corporation is dissolved or made insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Quebec corporation with no real employees, assets, or decision-making, while using it to route video-chat royalties or dividends to a tax-haven intermediary solely for treaty abuse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA will invoke GAAR to deny treaty benefits and re-characterise transactions; reassess tax, interest, and penalties; evidence of willfulness triggers tax evasion prosecution and fines of up to 200% of tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Fiscally, courts may pierce the corporate veil where the corporation is a sham; directors face civil restitution, asset seizures, forced compliance travel bans, and imprisonment under s. 239 ITA on criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / FINTRAC Violations in Payment Processing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a random video-matching app without registering as a Money Service Business (MSB), failing to establish a FINTRAC compliance program, or processing payments from Apple IAP / Paymentwall streams without adequate transaction monitoring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act penalties: administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 for entities (or CAD 500,000 for individuals); unregistered MSB fines of up to CAD 500,000 and/or six months' imprisonment on summary conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers may be held personally liable for directing or acquiescing in MSB non-compliance; criminal prosecution can lead to imprisonment, prohibition from managing corporations, and cross-border travel restrictions under enforcement orders.
